body.statement: For every \(\theta\in\Theta_S\), multiplication by \(p_\theta\) maps the fortified conditional-mean-zero functions bijectively onto the specialization of \(H_S\) and maps \(L^2(C)\) onto the specialization of \(R_S(x)\). Consequently, \(\operatorname{rank}M_\theta\) equals the rank of the composite block-column map \(\bigoplus_{y\in\mathcal I_S}\mathbb R^u\xrightarrow{\oplus_y\Pi_{\theta,y}}\mathbb R^S\to\mathbb R^S/N_S(p_\theta)\).
body.justification: This reduction removes law-dependent denominators and exposes the structural-zero problem as a product of block-subspace choices.
body.gap: Yu, Shi, and Tchetgen Tchetgen define the fortified conditional moments, but their finite illustration does not derive a support-incidence representation with heterogeneous alphabets and structural zeros.
body.consumer: The reduction gives a law-independent input to the Hall certificate and prevents a rank failure caused by support from being mistaken for weak association at one law.
